heading: INT. NATIONAL RESPONSE CALL CENTER, FLOOR THREE - DAY

units.text: INT. NATIONAL RESPONSE CALL CENTER, FLOOR THREE - DAY
Beige cubicles.
Gray carpet.
A banner: "EVERY CALL IS AN OPPORTUNITY!"
A wall clock ticks over a whiteboard of call counts.
DUANE PRESCOTT, 40s, in a headset and a tie loosened to the second button, sits at a cube with a script taped to the monitor.
SHANICE WILLIAMS, 30s, in the next cube, fills out a form in tiny block letters, never glancing up.
Thank you for calling National Response, my name is Duane. How may I...
units.name: DUANE

units.text: He stops.
Listens.
Writes a line.
Crosses it out.
Yes, ma'am, I understand your frustration.
units.name: DUANE

units.text: Shanice lowers her pen.
Duane. You've said "I understand" eleven times.
units.name: SHANICE

units.text: Because I do understand.
units.name: DUANE

units.text: You've been transferred to nobody.
units.name: SHANICE

units.text: A chirp from the ceiling speaker.
The intercom.
Attention, floor three. This is a reminder that average handle time is up four percent. Please be mindful.
units.name: KOVACS

units.text: Mindful. I'm mindful.
units.name: DUANE

units.text: Four percent. We're a ship and it's four percent.
units.name: SHANICE

units.text: A few muffled snorts from nearby cubes.
Duane slides his chair back.
Shanice stands.
They look at each other over the cubicle wall, then at the clock.
Also, Duane. Shanice. Please remember that personal conversations are logged.
units.name: KOVACS

units.text: Duane takes off his headset and places it in the middle of his desk.
Shanice does the same.
Together they push back their chairs, which squeal on the carpet.
Mr. Kovacs, I have a question.
units.name: DUANE

units.text: Please direct it to your supervisor.
units.name: KOVACS

units.text: You are my supervisor.
units.name: DUANE

units.text: Then please direct it to a future me.
units.name: KOVACS

units.text: Shanice walks to the banner and takes a corner in each fist.
The tape tears loose with a long squeal.
Duane takes hold of the other end.
They bring it down and stand there in a slump of paper, holding it between them.
I always hated that banner.
units.name: SHANICE

units.text: I wrote it.
units.name: DUANE

units.text: I know.
units.name: SHANICE

units.text: The intercom chirps again, but neither of them listens.
